audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Ryze Levels 1 through 5 at 7-8/10 while the whys under those exact rows describe Mundo controlling the lane, out-regenerating the poke, and Ryze accepting a CS deficit. It also labels a 43.49% matchup "Even — difficulty 5.5/10" with the amber tone.
audit.why: The mirror (drmundo__ryze) already fixed this chart to Levels 1-3 Dr. Mundo, Levels 4-5 Ryze, Level 6 skill, first item Dr. Mundo, 2+ items Ryze, matching the packet and the prose. Ryze winning 43.5% of these is not an even lane.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 5 and 6 flipped in both layers as matched pairs to agree with the mirror, ratings moved with them, and difficulty raised to Hard 7.5/10 with carry threat 7/10 and the tone token moved off amber.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet reports sequencingCues 0, and spikes[1] claims Maximum Dosage "heals a massive chunk" while mid puts a number on it — "heals 20-25% of his max HP instantly".
audit.why: Riot's text: Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percentage of his *missing* health, then regenerates a portion of maximum health over a long duration, on a flat 120s. Missing-health scaling is the opposite of the max-health figure the page invented — the lower you push him, the more it returns, which changes how you bait it.
audit.corrected: Invented percentages removed and replaced with the missing-health mechanic plus the flat 120s; Heart Zapper's 15-17s and Infected Bonesaw's flat 4s written in as the actual sequencing cues.
sources: champ-data/_kits/drmundo.json (R cd 120, text; W 17/16.5/16/15.5/15; Q cd 4, range 975)

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors repeated across the page. Heart Zapper is called (E) and described as a bonus-damage auto proc. Infected Bonesaw is repeatedly called "Cleaver". And Goes Where He Pleases — the passive that resists Ryze's first immobilising effect outright — is described only as regeneration, never as the thing that eats the root the entire game plan depends on.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is W: he electrocutes himself, stores a portion of the damage he takes, then bursts nearby enemies at 325 and heals off the stored damage. Blunt Force Trauma is E, and that is the auto reset. Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilising effect, costing him health and dropping a cannister he can walk over to heal and reduce the passive's cooldown — so the first Rune Prison Ryze lands does nothing but feed him a heal. That is the decisive interaction in this matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper restored to W with its 325 radius and store-then-heal mechanic, Blunt Force Trauma named as the auto reset, Infected Bonesaw used throughout, and the passive's root-shrug written in as the reason to bait before you root.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] says Mundo drains health "through your mana-shield sustain".
audit.why: Ryze has no shield. Arcane Mastery turns bonus mana into spell damage and AP into maximum mana — nothing absorbs anything.
audit.corrected: Shield removed; the line now says what actually happens, which is that Infected Bonesaw outranges every tool Ryze could answer with.

edits.before: Dr. Mundo's Infected Bonesaw (Q) is a percent-current-HP missile you must play around from level 1 — it hits for roughly 20% of your current HP each cast and he throws it every four seconds, so letting him land three in a row through the wave puts you in kill range before you even have W. Stand behind a minion cluster when he winds up; his Q travels in a straight line and a single creep body blocks it. Your only level 1 trade is Q from max range, and even that is a wash — he heals the damage back through his passive rupture regeneration. At level 2, W root gives you a threat, but spending it forces you melee-close where Heart Zapper (E) bonus damage fires automatically on his next auto — you will trade poorly. At level 3 your Flux bounce loop is online, but Mundo shrugs poke with his passive: you need three or four full E-Q-W rotations to move his bar, and he will land two Cleavers on you in that time. Accept this: early lane is his. Farm, sidestep Cleavers, and do not burn Flash trying to prove a point.
edits.after: Infected Bonesaw is a current-health missile you play around from level 1 — free to cast, 975 range, back every four seconds, so three in a row through the wave puts you in kill range before you even have Rune Prison. Stand behind a minion cluster when he winds up; it hits the first enemy in a line and one creep body eats it. Your level 1 answer is Overload from max range, and it is a wash because Goes Where He Pleases regenerates it back. At level 2 the root looks like a threat, but the same passive resists your first immobilising effect entirely and drops a cannister that heals him — bait that shrug before the root you actually need. At level 3 your Flux loop is online and still too slow: several full rotations to move his bar, two Bonesaws landed on you meanwhile. Early lane is his. Farm, sidestep, and do not spend Flash proving otherwise.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are a managed stalemate where your job is CS efficiency and mana banking. His Q damage scales with your max HP as you build mana items, so the more you stack toward Seraph's, the harder each Cleaver hurts in percentage terms — respect it. At level 6 he gets Maximum Dosage (R): if you have him to 20% HP and burn your combo, he presses R, heals 20-25% of his max HP instantly, gains a large movement speed steroid, and runs you down. Do not attempt an all-in at 6 unless he has already used R. Use Realm Warp defensively — it is your escape valve if he gets snowballing or if their jungler appears, since you have no dash to disengage otherwise. The correct mid-game play is to accept a slight CS deficit if it means avoiding a Cleaver that puts you in lethal range, then look for a roam or warp opportunity rather than grinding a losing 1v1.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are a managed stalemate where your job is CS efficiency and mana banking. Infected Bonesaw scales off your current health, so it hurts most exactly when you are already low — respect it at every health total, not just full. At level 6 he gets Maximum Dosage on a flat 120 seconds: it instantly heals a share of his *missing* health and then regenerates more over a long duration, so pushing him to 20% makes the heal bigger, not smaller, and the speed bonus lets him chase. Never all-in at 6 unless it is already spent. Realm Warp is your escape valve, not a combat spike — you have no dash. Take the small CS deficit over the Bonesaw that puts you in lethal range.

notes: The decisive interaction in this matchup was missing entirely: Goes Where He Pleases resists Ryze's first immobilising effect, drops a cannister that heals Mundo and refunds passive cooldown when he walks over it. Ryze's whole game plan is Flux-then-Rune Prison, so the first root is always wasted — bait it out before the one you need. Also corrected: Heart Zapper is W (325-range store-and-burst self-electrocution), not an E auto-proc; Blunt Force Trauma (E) is the auto reset; 'Cleaver' is not the name of anything in this kit; and Maximum Dosage heals off *missing* health, which the page had as 20-25% of maximum. The page also gave Ryze a 'mana-shield' he does not have. Difficulty was labelled Even on a 43.49% matchup and is now Hard.
